difficultyRationale: Platform-estimated: a single spatial skill (reassembling four pieces in their natural positions) followed by a direct visual comparison of four figures; about 1 to 1.5 min for a prepared student.
stem:
The four pieces of a puzzle are shown in the figure below.

![Figure: Four black puzzle pieces. Each is a triangle cut from one side of a square along its diagonals (left, top, right and bottom), with notches along its inner edges: the left piece has a concave arc and a small step, the top piece has a round bite, the right piece has a long thin spike-shaped notch and a step, and the bottom piece has a zigzag top edge with two peaks.](/pyq/2026/fig/Q03-1.png)

Which one of the figures labelled as P, Q, R, and S can be constructed by using each of the four pieces only once without overlaps?

![Figure: Four black squares labelled P, Q, R and S, each with a white bird-like cut-out. P: round head, long thin beak pointing right and a tilted rectangular body. Q: round head with no beak and the same tilted body. R: head and beak as in P, but the body is cut off flat at the bottom. S: beak and tilted body as in P, but a black V-shaped wedge cuts into the top of the head.](/pyq/2026/fig/Q03-2.png)

solution.quick: Each piece is one of the four triangles you get by cutting a square along both diagonals, so the pieces must form a square frame, each on "its" side (left, top, right, bottom). Put together as drawn, their notches leave a white hole shaped like a bird: a round head, a long thin beak pointing right and a tilted rectangular body. That is exactly figure **P**, so the answer is **(A)**.

steps.title: Read the pieces
steps.body:
Every piece has one long straight outer edge with 45° ends: it is one of the four triangles obtained by cutting a square along **both diagonals**, with parts of its inner (diagonal) edges cut away.

- **Left piece**: straight edge on the left; its inner edges have a concave arc and a small step.
- **Top piece**: straight edge on top; its inner edges have a round bite.
- **Right piece**: straight edge on the right; its inner edges have a long, thin spike-shaped notch and a small step.
- **Bottom piece**: straight edge at the bottom; its top edge is a zigzag with a small left peak, a V-shaped dip and a larger right peak.

steps.title: Assemble the square
steps.body: All four answer figures have a complete black square as their outer boundary. Each piece has exactly one straight edge as long as a side of that square, so each piece must lie with its straight edge along one side, as the four triangles of the diagonally cut square. The pieces are drawn already in these orientations, so place them exactly as drawn: left piece on the left, top on top, right on the right, bottom at the bottom.

steps.title: Work out the white hole that remains
Compare with P, Q, R and S
steps.body:
| Figure | Head | Beak | Body | Can be built? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P | round | long, thin, pointing right | tilted, with a pointed lowest corner | **Yes**: matches exactly |
| Q | round, flattened on the right | **missing** | tilted | No: the right piece's beak notch must leave a white beak |
| R | round | present | **cut off flat** at the bottom | No: the V-dip of the bottom piece must leave the pointed lowest corner white |
| S | **black wedge** cut into its top | present | tilted | No: the top piece's bite is a smooth arc and no piece supplies that wedge |

steps.title: Area check and conclusion
steps.body: Using each piece once without overlaps, the black area of the finished square must equal the total area of the four pieces. Q, R and S each have **extra black** (where the beak, the lower corner of the body, or part of the head should be white), so they would need more material than the four pieces provide. Only **P** can be constructed, so the answer is **(A)**.

solution.teaching:
**Assembly (jigsaw) puzzles in spatial aptitude.** These questions give you a few pieces and ask which target figure they can form. Three principles make them quick and reliable.

1. **Use the outer boundary first.** Straight edges, right angles and corners must lie on the boundary of the target. Here every piece has one long straight edge with 45° ends, i.e. it is one of the four triangles you get when a square is cut along both diagonals. The target is a full square, so the four pieces must sit one on each side, meeting at the centre along the diagonals. The layout is fixed; only the details of the inner edges vary.
2. **Every notch shows up.** Pieces cannot overlap, so a notch cut into a piece stays empty in the final figure, and a black region in the target must be covered by some piece. A good habit is to list each distinctive notch (here: round bite, spike-shaped notch, V-shaped dip) and check that each target shows it in the right place.
3. **Conservation of area.** Using every piece exactly once without overlaps means the total black area is fixed. A target with more black (a smaller hole) or less black (a larger hole) than the pieces supply is impossible.

Rotation and reflection are allowed in principle, but here the square boundary forces each piece onto one side, and the pieces are already drawn in the orientation of their own side, so the natural arrangement is the only one worth testing.

**In this question**, the notches combine into a round head (left arc + top bite), a thin beak (right spike notch) and a tilted body whose lowest corner sits in the bottom piece's V. P shows all three; Q lacks the beak, R lacks the pointed lower corner, and S has an extra black wedge in the head. So only **P** works.

optionAnalysis.label: A
optionAnalysis.explanation: **P** shows exactly the hole the four pieces leave: a round head, a long thin beak pointing right, and a tilted body whose lowest corner falls in the V-dip of the bottom piece. A pixel overlay of the printed pieces reproduces P exactly.

optionAnalysis.label: B
optionAnalysis.explanation: **Q** has no beak (and a flattened right side of the head). The right piece has a long spike-shaped notch, which must leave a white beak, so Q cannot be formed.

optionAnalysis.label: C
optionAnalysis.explanation: **R** has its body cut off flat at the bottom. The bottom piece has a V-shaped dip that leaves the pointed lowest corner of the body white, so R would need extra black that no piece provides.

optionAnalysis.label: D
optionAnalysis.explanation: **S** has a black V-shaped wedge cutting into the top of the head. The top piece's bite is a smooth round arc and no piece has a wedge-shaped projection there, so S cannot be formed.

solution.shortcut: Pick the most distinctive notch in each piece and check it in each figure: the spike notch of the right piece forces a beak (eliminates Q), the smooth round bite of the top piece forces a full round head (eliminates S), and the V-dip of the bottom piece forces a pointed lower corner (eliminates R).
solution.commonTrap: Judging only the overall silhouette (head plus body). Q, R and S differ from P in small details (missing beak, flat bottom, wedge in the head), so check every notch of every piece against the figure.

transcription.notes: Single-pass transcription from the official paper rendering; awaiting independent check. The two figures (the four pieces, and the four candidate figures P, Q, R, S with their labels) are cropped from the official page rendering. Only the faint background watermark was whitened (pixels with every channel at least 225 set to white); no figure content was altered. In the paper P and Q are in the top row and R and S in the bottom row, as reproduced. The second official image is the top of page 3 (header and table border only).

answerVerification.method: Author solve (not blind) compared with official key
answerVerification.checkCode:
# Q3: put the 4 printed pieces back into one square; compare with P,Q,R,S (run from repo root)
from PIL import Image; import numpy as np
L=lambda f: np.array(Image.open(f).convert('L'))<128
A=L('public/pyq/2026/fig/Q03-1.png'); B=L('public/pyq/2026/fig/Q03-2.png')
c=np.where(A.any(0))[0]; G=np.split(c,np.where(np.diff(c)>1)[0]+1)  # pieces: left, top, right, bottom
r=np.where(A[:,G[0][0]:G[0][-1]+1].any(1))[0]; y0,s=r[0],r[-1]-r[0]+1  # left piece spans a full side
U=np.zeros((s,s),bool)
for k,g in enumerate(G):
    P=np.zeros_like(A); P[:,g[0]:g[-1]+1]=A[:,g[0]:g[-1]+1]
    x0=g[-1]-s+1 if k==2 else g[0]; U|=P[y0:y0+s,x0:x0+s]
def bands(v,t):
    i=np.where(v>t)[0]; return [(b[0],b[-1]+1) for b in np.split(i,np.where(np.diff(i)>1)[0]+1)]
res={}
for ri,(a,b) in enumerate(bands(B.sum(1),60)):
    for ci,(p,q) in enumerate(bands(B[a:b].sum(0),0)):
        M=np.array(Image.fromarray(B[a:b,p:q]).resize((s,s)))!=U
        for _ in range(2): M=M[1:-1,1:-1]&M[:-2,1:-1]&M[2:,1:-1]&M[1:-1,:-2]&M[1:-1,2:]  # drop 1-2px seams
        res['PQRS'[2*ri+ci]]=int(M.sum())
print(res)  # expect P: 0 (exact fit); Q, R, S: large solid mismatches
answerVerification.notes: Visual solve: the pieces placed in their natural positions leave a head + beak + tilted body hole identical to P. Checked with a pixel overlay of the pieces as printed (piece images also extracted from the PDF gave the same result): after removing 1–2 px seams, the mismatch with P is 0 px, while Q, R and S differ by solid regions (the beak, the lower part of the body, a wedge in the head). Matches the official key (A).
